name: Homeowner
whoTheyAre: Building or renovating their own home, first- or second-time buyer of interior materials.
whatTheyBuy: Small mixed lists — laminate shade, plywood sheets, hardware, adhesive.
whyTheyBuy: Renovation or new-build interior fit-out starting; often comparing against a carpenter's or contractor's quoted materials.
painPoints: No visibility into fair material pricing
Ten different dealer conversations to compare one BOQ
Uncertain which grade/thickness actually applies to their use case
buyingTriggers: Received a carpenter quote and wants to sanity-check material cost
objections: Is this actually cheaper than my carpenter's supplier?
Can I trust an online quote for something this expensive?
trustSignals: Transparent per-sq.ft rates shown before contact
Real product photos and shade codes
Certifications visible on the product page
recommendedOffer: Get My Quote on a specific price-list page (e.g. plywood-price, laminate-price)
bestCta: Compare real prices before you commit to a carpenter's quote.
relevantContent: Grade comparison tables (MR vs BWR vs BWP vs FR)

name: Carpenter
whoTheyAre: Independent tradesperson executing client jobs, orders material per active job.
whatTheyBuy: Repeat small-to-mid orders, brand/grade-specific, often shade-code exact.
whyTheyBuy: An active job needs material today or this week.
painPoints: Exact shade/code match across a job
Stock reliability — can't afford a delayed delivery mid-job
buyingTriggers: Existing job needs a matching restock
objections: Will delivery actually be same/next-day as promised?
Is the shade code exactly what I specified?
bestCta: Send the shade codes, get today's rate.

name: Interior Contractor
whoTheyAre: Runs multiple residential/commercial interior jobs concurrently.
whyTheyBuy: New project signed, needs a supplier who won't be the bottleneck on a tight timeline.
painPoints: Reconciling quotes from five different vendors in five formats
Project delays from a single missing material line
buyingTriggers: Existing supplier underperforming on lead time
objections: Can one supplier really cover every category on my BOQ?
What happens if something's out of stock mid-project?
bestCta: Send your BOQ. Get one quote, not five.

name: Turnkey Contractor
whoTheyAre: Owns full project delivery, material cost is a fixed-price liability.
whatTheyBuy: Full-project material lists across every category, front-loaded.
whyTheyBuy: Project kickoff; needs to lock material cost early to protect margin on a fixed-price contract.
painPoints: Price volatility eating margin on a fixed-price job
No single accountable supplier for the whole material scope
objections: Can pricing be locked for the project duration?
Who do I call when something goes wrong — one number or five?
bestCta: Project procurement without calling ten suppliers.

name: Architect
whoTheyAre: Specifies materials for a client project, not always the buyer.
whatTheyBuy: Spec-driven — certifications, grades, finish codes referenced in drawings.
whyTheyBuy: Specifying materials for a client project; needs a source they can point the client/contractor to.
painPoints: Needs certification/spec detail, not just a price
Wants confidence the spec'd product is actually available
buyingTriggers: Drafting a materials schedule for a project
objections: Will this exact spec be in stock when the contractor orders?
trustSignals: IS certification detail on every board/plywood page
bestCta: Transparent specs and certifications, not just a price list.

name: Interior Designer
whoTheyAre: Presents material and finish options to a client for approval.
whatTheyBuy: Shade/finish-led — laminate, veneer, solid surface, chosen for the room, not the spec sheet.
whyTheyBuy: Presenting material options to a client for sign-off.
painPoints: Needs a real shade catalogue with accurate images, not a swatch book
Client changes mind — needs fast alternative options
buyingTriggers: Client requested change to a finish
objections: Do the photos match the actual shade in person?
Can availability be confirmed before I present it?
recommendedOffer: Shade catalogue browse + same-day rate confirmation
bestCta: Real shade catalogue with codes, images, and today's rate.

name: Builder
whoTheyAre: Construction-side, ongoing sites needing consistent restock.
painPoints: Grade consistency across bulk orders
Volume pricing not always transparent
objections: Is bulk pricing actually better than my current supplier?
bestCta: Send the sheet count. Get a volume rate.

name: Retail Rollout Company
whoTheyAre: Opens multiple outlets against a fixed fit-out template.
whatTheyBuy: Standardised material kits, repeated per site.
whyTheyBuy: Opening multiple outlets on a template fit-out; needs the same spec reproduced reliably.
painPoints: Re-sourcing the same spec for every new site is wasted effort
Inconsistent material quality between sites damages brand consistency
objections: Can EightByFour support a multi-site rollout, not just one job?
bestCta: One procurement partner across every site, not a new vendor search each time.

name: Hospitality Project Team
whoTheyAre: Fit-out or renovation team on a hard deadline (opening date, event).
whyTheyBuy: Fit-out or renovation on a hard deadline.
painPoints: Any material delay threatens the opening date
Coordinating multiple vendors under time pressure
objections: Can delivery genuinely be guaranteed against our deadline?
bestCta: Reliability + consolidated procurement under time pressure.

name: Commercial Project Team
whoTheyAre: Office/commercial fit-out, often with a compliance-driven spec sheet.
whyTheyBuy: Office/commercial fit-out with a spec sheet to satisfy.
painPoints: Compliance verification across every material line
Single point of accountability for a mixed-category spec
objections: Does every SKU in the quote actually carry the required certification?
trustSignals: IS 5509 / IS 710 certification detail per product

name: Outstation company executing locally
whoTheyAre: Company with no existing Hyderabad supplier relationships, executing a project in the city.
whatTheyBuy: Full project lists, no local supplier relationships to fall back on.
whyTheyBuy: Executing a project in Hyderabad without local sourcing contacts.
painPoints: No local supplier network to vet
Doesn't know local sizing/stocking conventions (e.g. nominal vs actual thickness)
buyingTriggers: Won a project outside their home market
objections: Can we trust a local partner we've never worked with before?
bestCta: EightByFour is your local material procurement desk — you don't need a Hyderabad contact of your own.
